about: Every spacecraft that tried to land on Mars and reached its atmosphere, 1971–2021. Coordinates are planetocentric, degrees east (lon_e, 0–360) and −180–180 (lon), from each Wikipedia article. Mars 2's crash site is an estimate and Mars Polar Lander's is its target. Not included: Mars 7's lander (missed the planet), Deep Space 2 (two impactor probes lost with Mars Polar Lander), and missions that never left Earth orbit (Mars 96, Fobos-Grunt).

landings.name: Mars 2
landings.what_happened: Entered too steeply and crashed: the first human-made object on Mars. The crash site is an estimate.

landings.name: Mars 3
landings.what_happened: The first soft landing on Mars. It went silent shortly after touching down, during a global dust storm.

landings.name: Mars 6
landings.what_happened: Sent back data from the atmosphere on the way down, but contact was lost just before touchdown.

landings.name: Viking 1
landings.what_happened: The first lander to work on Mars, and for more than six years. Released from orbit after a month of looking for a safe site.

landings.name: Viking 2
landings.what_happened: Worked for three and a half years; photographed frost on the ground in winter.

landings.name: Pathfinder
landings.what_happened: Faster, better, cheaper: three years and under $150 million for the lander. Carried Sojourner, the first rover to drive on Mars.

landings.name: Mars Polar Lander
landings.what_happened: Lost during descent, most likely because it shut its engines off too early. The position is the target, not a found site.

landings.name: Beagle 2
landings.what_happened: Landed but never called home. Found in 2015 in orbiter images: its solar panels had not fully opened.

landings.name: Spirit
landings.what_happened: Planned for 90 sols, drove for six years until it got stuck in soft sand.

landings.name: Opportunity
landings.what_happened: Planned for 90 sols, worked for more than 14 years and drove 45 km, until a dust storm covered its solar panels.

landings.name: Phoenix
landings.what_happened: Landed in the Arctic and dug up water ice; ended when the polar winter came.

landings.name: Curiosity
landings.what_happened: Too heavy for airbags: lowered on cables by a rocket-powered sky crane. Still climbing Mount Sharp.

landings.name: Schiaparelli
landings.what_happened: A test lander. A sensor glitch made it think it was already on the ground, so it cut its engines early and crashed.

landings.name: InSight
landings.what_happened: A geophysics station: recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes until dust ended its power.

landings.name: Perseverance
landings.what_happened: Sky crane again. Collects rock samples for a later return to Earth, and carried Ingenuity, the first helicopter on another planet.

landings.name: Zhurong
landings.what_happened: China's first Mars landing, at the first try. The rover went to sleep for the winter in May 2022 and has not woken up.
